item.title: Read and listen to more for less with a Black Library app subscription
item.description: Unlock credits for Black Library stories with a new subscription offer.
item.content:encoded:
Do you love Black Library novels? Need to catch up on some fan-favourite series? Now you’ll be able to pick up your most sought-after stories for less with a new Black Library app subscription.

This new, optional subscription service gives you credits that you can redeem for any of the thousands of stories living in the Black Library app, whether you’re looking to start the epic Siege of Terra series or want to check in with Ciaphas Cain’s latest escapade. 

Whether you're an ebook reader or prefer to listen to your literature, there are a separate subscription packages for audiobooks and ebooks,* so you can choose exactly what you want – and save money doing it. Both will be available monthly or annually, and if you want to get the most out of your credits, annual is the way to go.

Both plans get one credit per month, but annual subscribers get all 12 of theirs up-front, while also saving money compared to a monthly subscription. Annual subscribers can also purchase additional credits whenever they like, in case a particular novel or audiobook is too good to wait for.

All subscribers also unlock access to free monthly content, which matches your subscription type – audio for audiobook subscribers, eShorts and eBooks for eBook subscribers, with eBook releases available in French and German as well as English. 

Monthly subscribers will get access to free content released while their membership is active, while annual subscribers get back catalogue access to everything that’s come before as a cherry on top.** 

Want a sneak preview of the first month’s free content? Things kick off with the first part of a brand new four-part serial, Azrael: Sword of Secrets by Gary Kloster. Follow the Supreme Grand Master of the Dark Angels as he finds the balance of his life changed and he has to deal with a new feeling – doubt.

Non-subscribers can keep using the Black Library app as normal – but if you find yourself diving into the Black Library shelves for a new adventure every month or two, you’ll want to give the new subscription a look.

The subscription service is live now, so log into the Black Library App and sign up today!

Download the app now

* Audiobook credits can’t be used to purchase eBooks, and vice versa.
** On launch, there won’t be a back catalogue, but it will soon build up.

item.title: New Armies of Renown rules for Seraphon
item.description: It’s not all doom and gloom with Blessed Tetaxi – see the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar rules.
item.content:encoded:
We’ve seen the army rules and some of the updated warscrolls from the new Seraphon battletome. Today, we’re taking a look at the two Armies of Renown from the book, and the characterful forces they unlock.

Envoys of Tepok

First off, we have the latest skink in town – Blessed Tetaxi – leading the Envoys of Tepok. This Army of Renown is built around a core of non-Monster skink units and Blessed Tetaxi’s attendant priests. Clearly nobody’s told these diminutive Seraphon that it’s not the end of the world as their Prevent the Coming Darkness battle trait sees them taking issue with any enemies they believe to be responsible for bringing about the apocalypse.

ENVOYS OF TEPOK

Passive

PREVENT THE COMING DARKNESS

Guided by their prophets, the skinks are possessed by a desperate energy in their mission to destroy those who would usher in the apocalypse.

Effect: While a friendly unit is prophesying doom:

  • Add 1 to chanting rolls for that unit.

  • Add 1 to run rolls for that unit.

  • That unit’s melee weapons have Crit (Auto-wound), including Companion weapons.

This doom-laden fanaticism stems from Blessed Tetaxi, who is the only unit to start the battle under the influence of these ill omens. This sort of hysteria tends to be catching, however, with the venerable skink able to influence nearby units who, in subsequent turns, will go on to afflict their comrades with an air of doom and gloom.*

ENVOYS OF TEPOK

Once Per Turn (Army), End of Any Turn

GROWING HYSTERIA

The skittish skinks fuel one another’s paranoid speculations.

Declare: For each friendly unit that is prophesying doom, pick another friendly ENVOYS OF TEPOK SKINK unit within 3" of them to be a target.

Effect: For each target, make a nervous muttering roll of D6. On a 4+, the target is prophesying doom for the rest of the battle.

The key to this force will be ensuring that early turns are spent on set-up –  spreading the effects of prophesying doom around so that when battlelines meet, your foes are met with skinks who pack a surprising punch. 

Blessed Tetaxi and other skink Priests in the army can make the most out of the new Prayer Lore. Start chanting Slay the Harbingers and mark an enemy unit as an omen of doom, making your units murderously effective against them in combat. Fast striking units such as Raptadon Chargers will melt through these marked targets in no time. 

ENVOYS OF TEPOK

Your Hero Phase

SLAY THE HARBINGERS

Those identified as omens of the coming doom by Tetaxi and his fellow priests must be cut down with all haste, for surely doing so is the only way disaster might just be prevented!

Declare: Pick a friendly ENVOYS OF TEPOK PRIEST to chant this prayer, pick a visible enemy unit within 12" of them to be the target, then make a chanting roll of D6.

Effect: If there are no enemy omens of doom on the battlefield, the target is an omen of doom for the rest of the battle.

Until the start of your next turn, add 1 to hit rolls for combat attacks made by friendly ENVOYS OF TEPOK units that target an omen of doom. In addition, if the chanting roll was 8+, until the start of your next turn, add 1 to wound rolls for combat attacks made by friendly ENVOYS OF TEPOK units that target an omen of doom.

KEYWORDS: PRAYER

Another prayer – Let Tepok Be Our Guide – adds 2” to the Move characteristic of a selected unit, which is handy for the single unit of Kroxigor you can take in the army, or for making your Raptadon Chargers even faster. 

Of course, all of this doom and gloom could just be a massive conspiracy. Fortunately, one of your skinks can don the Starfoil Helm to ensure that nearby units don’t have any doubts.

ENVOYS OF TEPOK

Passive

STARFOIL HELM

This shining, peaked helm marks the bearer as Tetaxi’s second in command; all followers of Tepok carefully heed their words, for they are surely privy to the inner thoughts of the prophet.

Effect: Add 1 to nervous muttering rolls made for targets of the ‘Growing Hysteria’ ability if that target is wholly within 12" of and visible to this unit.

Starborne Warhost

Meanwhile, the Starborne Warhost have looked at what’s written in the stars and it doesn’t look too promising for any enemies of the Seraphon.

This new Army of Renown is all about getting into the flow of things. With the new Stellar Conjunction battle trait, the army divides the battlefield into a stellar map of your choosing, with Celestial Nodes marking out astral leylines.

STARBORNE WARHOST

Once Per Turn (Army), Deployment Phase

STELLAR CONJUNCTION

The Starborne seek to restore the flow of magic in the ley lines to harness the power of the Old Ones. Known to few but the slann, the terrestrial nodes in these lines have celestial counterparts…

Effect: Pick 1 of the following star maps to shine on the battlefield for the rest of the battle. The long and short edges of the star map align with the long and short edges of the battlefield. You can choose the orientation of the star map. Set up a flat 40mm celestial node in each of the locations depicted by a <Icon>  on the star map you picked.

Aligning your forces with the Celestial Nodes unlocks a host of benefits for your army, making it worthwhile to plan the movement of your units with this in mind. In fact, you probably need a Great Plan…

This army introduces 3 new Asterisms for you to utilise, each unlocking new tools for your units. Take Xholankha’s Wanderings, for example, which folds reality around friendly Seraphon units deployed near Celestial Nodes, allowing them to strike from unseen quarters.

STARBORNE WARHOST

Once Per Turn (Army), Your Hero Phase

XHOLANKHA’S WANDERINGS

Reality around a group of Seraphon folds like the workings of an intricate puzzle box, before they suddenly reappear elsewhere.

Declare: You can use this ability if you have not used any other Asterism abilities this turn. Pick a friendly STARBORNE unit wholly within 9" of a friendly celestial node to be the target.

Effect: Remove the target from the battlefield and set it up again wholly within 6" of a different celestial node and more than 9" from all enemy units.

If you want to show off your mastery of the heavens, why not give the Nexus Bore to one of your Heroes? This powerful artefact allows a Seraphon character to siphon the power from a nearby node, removing it from the battlefield in exchange for powerful melee buffs to nearby units.

STARBORNE WARHOST

Any Combat Phase

NEXUS BORE

When held above an arcane nexus, this golden octahedron leaps from the bearer’s hand and thrusts a spiked protrusion into the ground. Unfurling like a flower, it channels the power of the node into a temporary energy field that fills Seraphon with fearsome vigour.

Declare: Pick a friendly celestial node within 3" of this unit to be the source. Then, pick up to 3 friendly STARBORNE units wholly within 12" of the source to be the targets.

Effect: Remove the source from the battlefield. For the rest of the turn, the targets’ melee weapons have Crit (2 Hits), including Companion weapons.

And finally, for those of you with a penchant for cosmic lasers, the new spell, Geomantic Flare allows nearby Starborne Wizards to harness the power of a sun and transmit it through nearby Celestial Nodes.

STARBORNE WARHOST

Your Hero Phase

GEOMANTIC FLARE (6)

The slann causes the energies flowing along a ley line to erupt in a great flare akin to the rippling ejections of a sun, incinerating enemies directly above it.

Declare: Pick a friendly STARBORNE WIZARD to cast this spell, pick a friendly celestial node within 3" of them to be the emitter, then make a casting roll of 2D6.

Effect: Pick either another friendly celestial node or a point on the battlefield within 12" of the emitter to be the target. Then, draw a straight line between the target and the emitter. Inflict D3 mortal damage on each enemy unit the line passes across.

KEYWORDS: SPELL

If this taster of the new Armies of Renown has you feverishly formulating your own Great Plan, the new Seraphon battletome and Blessed Tetaxi will be available to pre-order from Saturday.

* This is the exact feeling that sweeps through WarCom Towers as an article deadline gets closer.

item.title: Fight underground battles in the new Path to Glory expansion
item.description: Get ready for frantic subterranean action with the new rules in Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks.
item.content:encoded:
The latest Path to Glory expansion for Warhammer Age of Sigmar – The Grymmpeaks – takes you into the abandoned hold of Karak Vanggaz. The book is available to pre-order from Saturday, so we’re unearthing some of the lore and rules within.

The lore

Karak Vanggaz, known as the Silver Karak, was the greatest of the duardin strongholds in the Grymmpeaks. During the Age of Chaos, the region’s holds were ransacked one by one, with the Khazalites either slaughtered or displaced. Eventually, the doom of the Silver Karak came from within as many of its populace fell to the worship of Hashut.

Much of Vanggaz was crushed under thousands of tons of rubble in a catastrophic seismic event caused by the conflict. Now, centuries later, many seek the treasures of the Silver Karak. Yet, other creatures now live in the dark, and the restless dead know no peace within the empty halls.

New paths

One of the key features of the Path to Glory game mode is the ability for your Heroes and other units to gain renown and follow various Paths which can unlock a range of immersive and useful skills. Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks introduces a host of new options, each evoking the distinctly subterranean nature of the latest setting.

As your forces steadily reclaim the ancient realm of Karak Vanggaz, you can take the Path of the Armourer, and unlock the resources and ability to craft Reinforced Gorgets. They’re ideal for helping your units weather incoming Deathshrieker Rocket Battery fire (or Oathkeeper Cannon fire, depending on whose side you’re on!)

PATH OF THE ARMOURER

Once Per Battle (Army), Deployment Phase

REINFORCED GORGETS

When flipped down, these heavy metal neck-plates protect against incoming fire.

Declare: Pick another visible friendly unit wholly within 12" of this unit to be the target.

Effect: For the rest of the battle, subtract 1 from the Rend characteristic of weapons used for shooting attacks that target that friendly unit.

Underground warfare

With the action in Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks taking place in the lightless depths beneath the mountains, it’s only appropriate that the new battle pack should introduce new rules for frantic subterranean combat. Battlefields will now include walls (both breachable and unbreachable), pillars, and chamonite ore. 

Of course, there’s no point in having breachable walls without an ability to breach them! The Breaking Through ability allows your warriors to shift the debris blocking the way ahead, allowing them to enter new areas of the karak. This opens up plenty of opportunities to attack your foes from unexpected angles.

Unsurprisingly, fighting deep underground means that light and visibility come at a premium. Generals would do well to prioritise mining precious seams of chamonite ore as they are crucial to victory in certain battleplans. The gleam of this realmstone can even help light even the darkest paths.

Passive

GLINT OF METAL IN THE DARK

A blue-white gleam gives away the presence of the realmstone of Chamon.

Effect: While a unit is contesting a chamonite ore objective, the effect of the ‘All-encompassing Darkness’ ability does not restrict the distance visibility can be drawn to models in that unit.

Designer’s Note: The unit is ‘lit up’ in the dark by the gleaming ore.

Passive

ALL-ENCOMPASSING DARKNESS

In the mines of Karak Vanggaz, the only certainty is the heavy pall of darkness that envelops all who enter.

Effect: For the purposes of visibility, observing models cannot draw visibility to other models more than 9" from them. However, for observing models from the following factions, this distance is 12" instead: IDONETH DEEPKIN, KHAZALITE HOLDS, HELSMITHS OF HASHUT, SKAVEN, FLESH-EATER COURTS, NIGHTHAUNT, SOULBLIGHT GRAVELORDS and GLOOMSPITE GITZ.

Designer’s Note: Some factions are better at seeing in the dark!

Centuries of abandonment means that Karak Vanggaz is overdue for a good airing out. Unfortunately for your forces, this means they will be forced to navigate a variety of booby traps and hazards. In underground battles each player places D3 hazard markers on the battlefield. When any unit gets too close, you randomly determine what the hazard is – beware the pernicious Mutagenic Slime.

Passive

MUTAGENIC SLIME

Oozing metallic slime drips from the rocky ceiling, altering the properties of weapons it comes into contact with.

Effect: Each time a CHANGE-TOUCHED unit declares a FIGHT ability, as a reaction, you must do the following:

  • Determine the Hit characteristic of each non‑Companion weapon used by that unit for that FIGHT ability by rolling a D6.

  • Determine the Wound characteristic of each non‑Companion weapon used by that unit for that FIGHT ability by rolling a D6.

Designer’s Note: For example, if you rolled a 2 for a weapon with a characteristic of 4+ on its profile, that characteristic would change to 2+.

New battleplans

Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks features 12 new battleplans for linked narrative battles, taking your forces from the winding, crystal-studded canyons that lead to Karak Vanggaz, to the famed Hall of the Silver Throne.

If you want to take things one step further and create your own narrative scenarios, Battlemines of Chamon is an all new battleplan generator designed to allow you to create bespoke battleplans both for use in one-off games or as part of a wider campaign.

Battlemines of Chamon allows you to randomly generate terrain, victory conditions and the various twists which can impact a battle, such as Parting Gift, which allows you to set up a hazard marker when a Hero is destroyed.

Once Per Battle (Army), Deployment Phase

PARTING GIFT

This hero leaves a nasty surprise for their enemies before drawing their final breath.

Declare: Pick a friendly HERO to be the target.

Effect: The first time the target is destroyed, before removing it from the battlefield, you can set up a hazard marker within 3" of it.

Artefacts and traits

Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks brings a host of new Heroic Traits and Artefacts of Power, along with unique spell and prayer lores for your forces to call upon in times of need.

Eye for Hidden Treasures is a fantastic trait for budding prospectors looking to sniff out extra seams of that crucial chamonite ore.

HEROIC TRAITS

Any Movement Phase

EYE FOR HIDDEN TREASURES

Often, those areas of a mine that are avoided because of the danger they pose harbour untouched resources by virtue of the same.

Declare: Pick a hazard marker within 12" of this unit and that has not been picked to be the target of this ability by you this battle to be the target.

Effect: Roll a dice. On a 6, set up a chamonite ore objective within 1" of the target, then remove the target from the battlefield.

Duardin aren’t afraid to call a spade a spade, as demonstrated by the potent Rusty Shovel you can equip your heroes with. Quite frankly, who doesn’t love the idea of hitting an enemy warrior over the head with a shovel?

ARTEFACTS OF POWER

Any Combat Phase

RUSTY SHOVEL

The edge of this ancient shovel is still deadly sharp.

Declare: Pick an enemy unit in combat with this unit to be the target.

Effect: Inflict D3 mortal damage on the target.

If you feel like casting aspersions on your opponent’s tactical prowess, Troglodyte Wit is a handy prayer which allows you to reduce your foes to their most mindless states, making it harder for them to control objectives.

LORE OF THE SUBTERRANEAN GODS

Your Hero Phase

TROGLODYTE WIT (4)

This prayer returns foes to an atavistic state, reducing them to a mindless echo of the crudest cave-dwelling monsters.

Declare: Pick a friendly PRIEST to chant this prayer, pick a visible enemy unit within 18" of them to be the target, then make a chanting roll of D6.

Effect: Until the start of your next turn, the target has a maximum control score of 1. If the chanting roll was 7+, in addition, until the start of your next turn, each time the target uses a command, unless your opponent spends 1 additional command point, the command has no effect, it still counts as

having been used and the command points spent to use the command are still lost.

KEYWORDS: PRAYER

That’s just a taste of what’s inside Path to Glory: The Grymmpeaks. There’ll be plenty more for you to unearth when the book goes on pre-order on Saturday. In the meantime, you can start planning your reclamation of Karak Vanggaz with the new Khazalite Holds range.

item.title: The Butcher’s Nails shreds its way onto Warhammer TV
item.description: Blood for the Blood God! Plus, authors, a quiz, and a bitter rivalry reignited on Battle Report.
item.content:encoded:
This week on Warhammer TV, The Butcher’s Nails makes its blood-soaked debut, fan-favourite author Chris Wraight chats about writing, and Battle Report hosts an Age of Darkness grudge match.

Available Friday: Hammer and Bolter – The Butcher’s Nails

The World Eaters are drawn to the far-flung rocky moon of Lamens by an ancient prophecy. As they launch their brutal attack… No, sorry, you’ll just have to wait until Friday to see what happens! We’ll have a full article dedicated to the blood-drenched Warhammer 40,000 animation when it launches.

We know you can feel the nails humming in your skull, but while you wait, you can enjoy these shows.

Available now: Scribes and Scriveners – Chris Wraight

From Warhammer Fantasy to the Vaults of Terra and The Scouring, few authors have had such a wide sweeping journey across the worlds of Warhammer as Chris Wraight. He joins host Alex on this week’s Scribes and Scriveners to talk about his extensive back catalogue, and to answer that crucial question for all authors – does he plan everything meticulously in advance?

Chris chats about his approach to writing and how easy it can be to become overwhelmed in the whole writing process. Watch now to enjoy a unique insight into the creative process of one of Black Library’s most prolific authors.

Available tomorrow: Brainboyz – Ork Speshul

Fink you’ve got a head full of Orky know-wots? Test your knowledge in a special edition of Brainboyz focusing entirely on the most brutal (and kunnin’) of the Warhammer 40,000 factions – the Orks.

If you know your Trukks from your Traktor Kannons, or think you can spot an Attack Squig from a thousand paces, why not tune in and see how you fare against our contestants in this noggin’ scratching quiz show. 

Available Thursday: Battle Report – Warhammer: The Horus Heresy


This week, Battle Report takes us to the galaxy-spanning battlefields of The Horus Heresy, throwing two forces into the claustrophobic and chaotic maelstrom of a Zone Mortalis engagement.

Regular viewers will recognise the generals from the 2025 edition of A Tale of Four Gamers. Quinn has returned with the noble Salamanders to take on Josh, who commands the malevolent Word Bearers. Both of these forces were the ones they built, painted, and played with a year ago, so it’s a great opportunity to see what tactical lessons the two generals have learnt in the last 12 months.

Coming Soon

There’s always more content coming to Warhammer TV. Just check out the Winter season trailer that we released last week:

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

All of that joins a staggering back catalogue of over 700 episodes including original animations, hobby guides and gaming content. Remember, your subscription also unlocks a host of premium features in the Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar apps, not to mention access to Warhammer Vault and a veritable treasure trove of lore books and articles.

If you subscribe for an entire year, you’ll also gain automatic entry into regular competitions, a copy of the Warhammer Yearbook and even a pair of special subscriber-only miniatures. If that wasn’t enough, an annual subscription nets you 12 months of content for the price of nine.

item.title: Warhammer Academy November content drop
item.description: See what new videos will be appearing on your playlists.
item.content:encoded:
Warhammer Academy is an essential online resource for anyone who wants to build confidence in their Warhammer skills, and there are more videos being added every month. 

This month, it’s time to go big as the might of both Imperial and Chaos Knights take centre stage. You can delve into the lore of both factions, including chivalric codes and the structure of knightly houses. There are also step-by-step tutorials for painting these towering war engines, helping you bring yours to life on the tabletop.

Away from Knights, we’ll also have lessons on how to paint your Combat Patrol Battlezone terrain as well as guides for basing your miniatures, and adding tufts and battlefield trophies to add that finishing touch.

There’s more to come in December, so check back next month.

Go to Warhammer Academy

If you’d like to learn these skills in person, you can head to your local Warhammer store where our friendly staff will be more than happy to help. Find your nearest store.

Speaking of which – from this week you’ll be able to earn a special achievement badge on Warhammer Academy by visiting a Warhammer store. Scan the code which is displayed in-store, and you’ll unlock the new Explorator badge.

item.title: New Seraphon warscrolls put astral power into your hands
item.description: See what the new skink character can do in your games of Warhammer Age of Sigmar.
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday, we saw how interpretations of the Great Plan are central to your new Seraphon army rules, but if you’re going to build your war host around them, you’ll need to know what your warriors do. Luckily, the prophets have granted us a peek at future warscrolls, so let’s see what they say.

Blessed Tetaxi

As the new skink on the block, Blessed Tetaxi is a good place to start. The Prophet of Tepok sits astride a mighty flying monster and channels the will of his god to predict which enemies carry dark omens – choosing one enemy unit within 12” in each of your Hero Phases. Tetaxi can invoke the Stone of Tehemundi to flood a foe’s mind with cosmic revelations, and if they’re his dark omen that turn, it’s even easier to slay one of their models outright.

DARK OMENS

Tetaxi’s mind is filled with visions of a coming Dark Day. When his visions clears, he hyper-focuses on one enemy, singling them out as the most pressing target of the moment.

Declare: Pick a visible enemy unit within 12" of this unit to be the target.

Effect: The target is a dark omen for the rest of the turn.

Your Hero Phase

THE STONE OF TEHEMUNDI (4)

Focusing upon the ovoid artefact he believes was gifted to him by Tepok, Tetaxi projects his visions into the minds of others. Few are able to withstand such an onslaught of cosmic truths.

Declare: Pick a visible enemy unit within 18" of this unit to be the target, then make a chanting roll of D6.

Effect: Roll a dice. If the target is a dark omen or the chanting roll was 8+, roll 2D6 instead. If the roll exceeds the target’s Health characteristic, 1 model in the target unit is slain.

KEYWORDS: PRAYER

You can also invoke an asterism* if the dark omen dies that turn, effectively adding an extra source of divine inspiration to your army rule.

Once Per Battle, End of Your Turn
TEPOK’S WILL

Guided by visions he believes are sent by Tepok, Tetaxi comes up with his own interpretations of the Great Plan. He is only tolerated by the slann as his predictions appear to be coming true.

Effect: If an enemy dark omen was destroyed this turn, pick 1 of the following asterisms to witness: ‘Coils of Sotek’, ‘Rays of Chotec’, ‘Jaws of Itzl’ or ‘Eye of Tepok’.

Kroxigor Warspawned

Need a way to ensure Tetaxi’s target shuffles off their mortal coil that turn? Bring some Kroxigor Warspawned to the party, whose weapons now hit for 3 and 4 Damage without needing an attendant skink unit nearby, while gaining an extra attack when charging or wrestling over an objective.

WARSPAWNED

While other kroxigor perform heavy labour, the Warspawned exist purely to kill and conquer in furtherance of the Great Plan.

Effect: If this unit charged this turn or this unit is contesting an objective you control, add 1 to the Attacks characteristic of this unit’s melee weapons for the rest of the turn.

Aggradon Lancers

Charging headlong into combat is great fun, and if anyone loves it more than kroxigors, it’s the Aggradon Lancers. They’re now more geared towards tearing through Infantry than shearing Monster hides, dealing mortal damage after charging and steadily healing to keep them in the fight for longer.

Aggradons rarely tire in battle; violence and bloodshed only serve to vitalise them and fuel their frenzy.

Effect: Each time this unit uses a Fight ability, after that ability has been resolved, Heal (D3) this unit.

Once Per Turn (Army), Any Charge Phase

SHREDDING CHARGE

Aggradons charge into combat in a storm of flashing fangs and talons.

Declare: If this unit charged this phase, pick an enemy unit within 1" of it to be the target.

Effect: Roll a dice for each model in this unit that is within 3" of the target. Add 1 to each roll if the target is INFANTRY. For each 4+, inflict 1 mortal damage on the target.

Engine of the Gods

We can’t have a skim through Seraphon warscrolls without seeing a massive reptilian beast, and the Engine of the Gods is one of the most impressive. It still serves as a locus for regenerating your fallen warriors – now drawing energy from nearby Priests to channel restorative magics – but gains a new role as a powerful centrepiece of support abilities, using asterisms you’ve beheld to enhance other Seraphon.

ENGINE OF THE GODS

Once Per Turn (Army), End of Any Turn

STARLIGHT SUMMONS

Memories of fallen Seraphon warriors coalesce from pure Azyrite magic into new physical forms.

Declare: Pick up to 3 visible friendly SERAPHON PRIESTS wholly within 12" of this unit to be the targets.

Effect: Remove any number of ritual points from the targets and give them to this unit. This unit can have a maximum of 6 ritual points. Then, pick a friendly SERAPHON unit wholly within 12" of this unit and return a number of slain models to it with a combined Health characteristic of up to the number of ritual points this unit has. Then, remove a number of ritual points from this unit equal to the combined Health characteristic of the models returned by this ability.

KEYWORDS: RAMPAGE

Passive

COSMIC ENGINE

The Engine of the Gods is a mysterious device capable of altering the natural laws of the universe.

Effect: For each of the following asterisms you have witnessed, apply the corresponding effect to friendly SERAPHON units while they are wholly within 12" of this unit:

Coils of Sotek: Add 3 to the control scores of those units.

Rays of Chotec: Add 1 to run rolls for those units.

Jaws of Itzl: Add 1 to wound rolls for combat attacks made by those units while they have not charged in the same turn.

Eye of Tepok: Add 1 to unbinding rolls for those units.

item.title: Enact the Great Plan with new Seraphon army rules
item.description: Take a look at some of the new rules dropping with Battletome: Seraphon.
item.content:encoded:
Battletome: Seraphon is available to pre-order this weekend. The heavens have aligned to allow us a sneak peek at the upcoming army rules for everyone’s favourite cold-blooded warriors.

The Great Plan

The slann have a plan, and it’s up to Seraphon commanders to Interpret the Great Plan. There are five stages to the Great Plan, and you pick three when you build your army to form your own interpretation. Creating an army to hunt enemy Heroes? Destroy the Malefactor is probably the choice for you. Picking loads of Wizards and Priests? Awaken the Ley Lines is the way to go.

INTERPRET THE GREAT PLAN

During army composition, you must pick 3 of the following stages to form your interpretation of the Great Plan and record them on your army roster. During the battle, you will be aiming to complete these stages to receive the guidance of the Old Ones in the stars, unlocking powerful abilities for the rest of the battle.

Destroy the Malefactor: An enemy HERO has been destroyed this battle.

Restore the Astromatrix: There is a friendly SERAPHON unit wholly within 12" of each battlefield corner.

Awaken the Ley Lines: 5 or more spells cast or prayers chanted by friendly SERAPHON units, in any combination, have been successfully cast or answered this battle.

Scour the Corruption: There is a friendly SERAPHON unit contesting a terrain feature that you control, and that terrain feature is within enemy territory and not within friendly territory.

Protect the Realmshaper: It is the third battle round or later, there is a friendly Realmshaper Engine on the battlefield, and there are no enemy units within 6" of that friendly Realmshaper Engine.

Meeting the conditions of a stage of the Great Plan causes shifts in the firmament, which Seraphon forces interpret as a sign that they are on the true path. On the battlefield, these manifest as asterisms, powerful stellar alignments which can grant your army potent boons. 

You can witness one asterism for free at the start of the battle, and another for each condition of the Great Plan you meet, meaning you can easily cascade multiple asterism effects across your army. For example,  you can call on the Coils of Sotek to descend from the heavens and constrict enemy units, hampering their ability to fight.

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Battle Round (Army), Any Hero Phase

COILS OF SOTEK

Shimmering serpent-forms constrict the foe, hampering their assault.

Declare: You can only use this ability if you have witnessed the ‘Coils of Sotek’ asterism. Pick a friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target. If you have witnessed 3 or more asterisms, you can pick an additional friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target.

Effect: For each target, pick an enemy unit in combat with that target. For the rest of the turn, subtract 1 from the Attacks characteristic of melee weapons used by those enemy units while they are in combat with any of the targets.

KEYWORDS: ASTERISM

The Eye of Tepok is going to be a welcome sight for Seraphon players who have built their army around magic, granting a huge boost to casting or chanting rolls.

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Battle Round (Army), Any Hero Phase

EYE OF TEPOK

Iridescent winds swirl about the wisest of the Seraphon, enhancing their rituals and spellcasting.

Declare: You can only use this ability if you have witnessed the ‘Eye of Tepok’ asterism. Pick a friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target. If you have witnessed 3 or more asterisms, you can pick an additional friendly SERAPHON unit to be a target.

Effect: The next time each target uses a SPELL or PRAYER ability this turn, when making the casting roll or chanting roll, add 1 to the number of dice rolled, to a maximum of 3, then remove 1 dice of your choice and use the remaining dice as the roll.

KEYWORDS: ASTERISM

Spells, Prayers, and Artefacts

Speaking of Tepok, they’re likely to have their eye on the Lore of Celestial Manipulation, which introduces some new spells for Seraphon players, including Celestial Reinforcement which is perfect for when your forces are looking thin on the ground.

LORE OF CELESTIAL MANIPULATION

Your Hero Phase

CELESTIAL REINFORCEMENTS (7)

Casting their mind to a distant temple-ship or nearby temple-city, the slann summons fresh Seraphon to the battlefield in an eye-searing flash of light.

Declare: Pick a friendly SERAPHON WIZARD to cast this spell, pick a friendly non-HERO non-MONSTER SERAPHON unit that has been destroyed to be the target, then make a casting roll of 2D6. Subtract 1 from the casting roll if it is the enemy turn.

Effect: Set up a replacement unit with half the number of models from the target unit (rounding up) wholly within 12" of the caster and more than 9" from all enemy units.

KEYWORDS: SPELL

It’s worth noting that some units which were previously wizards have now had a slight career change with the latest battletome. The Skink Starseer, Skink Starpriest, and Skink Oracle on Troglodon are now Priests, which is quite handy considering there’s a brand new prayer lore accompanying the new rules.*

Bite of Chotec is particularly handy if you want to give your opponent a nasty surprise in melee.

PRAYERS TO THE OLD ONES

Your Hero Phase

BITE OF CHOTEC (4)

The priest beseeches the sun god Chotec to imbue the weapons of the Seraphon with his blessing, causing them to release incinerating bursts of solar energy when they strike true.

Declare: Pick a friendly SERAPHON PRIEST to chant this prayer, pick a visible friendly SERAPHON unit wholly within 12" of them to be the target, then make a chanting roll of D6.

Effect: If the chanting roll was 8+, you can pick another eligible unit to be a second target. Until the start of your next hero phase, the targets’ melee weapons have Crit (2 Hits).

KEYWORDS: PRAYER, UNLIMITED

As is to be expected, the battletome also introduces a number of new Battle Formations, Heroic Traits, and Artefacts of Power for Seraphon players. The Crest of Chotec** is a great choice for those of you who love firing off celestial laser beams (and let’s face it, who doesn’t?).

TREASURES OF THE OLD ONES

Your Shooting Phase

CREST OF CHOTEC

This shimmering feathered headdress, inset with a brilliant carnelian gem, can loose an incinerating beam that burns with the heat of a star’s core.

Declare: Pick a point on the battlefield within 6" of this unit to be the target. Add 2" to the range for each asterism you have witnessed.

Effect: Draw a straight line between the target and the closest part on this unit’s base. Roll a D3 for each unit (friendly and enemy) that the line passes across. On a 2+, inflict an amount of mortal damage on that unit equal to the roll.

The new battletome is available for pre-order from Saturday. In the meantime, keep your eye on the heavens (or more specifically Warhammer Community) as later in the week we’ll be taking a look at some updated warscrolls for the Seraphon and their new Armies of Renown rules.

* Almost like it’s all been planned…
** Blimey, Chotec has been name dropped quite a lot. For those of you who aren’t in the knowtec, he is the Seraphon god of the sun and general representative of everything bright and burny.

item.title: More Battle March armies from the Warhammer: The Old World team
item.description: Get inspired by more forces for the smaller scale, fast-paced game mode.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier in the year, we showed off some incredible Battle March armies from the team behind Warhammer: The Old World. They’ve been busy painting more, and with the Tomb Kings of Khemri Battle March going up for pre-order tomorrow, now’s a great time to show them off.

Dominik – Warriors of Chaos

When planning this army, I knew I wanted to paint a force dedicated to Khorne, the Bloodied Hound as he’s called in Norsca. Inspired by classic Warhammer armies, I painted the army bright red with lots of gold trim. The bone-coloured helmets break this up and help to draw the eye to the focal point of the models.

With a Battle March army completed, I plan to expand the army with large units of Chaos Marauders and Marauder Horsemen, before finally adding a Chaos Dragon.

David – Warriors of Chaos

To paint the large areas of armour on my models, I started with a basecoat of Leadbelcher, over which I painted Black Templar Contrast paint to give them an oily, grimy feel, perfect for Warriors who’ve marched all the way from the Shard Lands to make war upon the Old World. For the fur coats and smaller details, I started by drybrushing on my base coats, over which I used a combination of Contrast paints and washes to add depth, before finally picking out the smaller details to tie everything together.

I’ve got plans to expand this army to 2,000 points or more, but unlike Dom I won’t be waiting to paint my Chaos Dragon – that’s the next model in my painting queue!

Dave – Grand Cathay

Inspired by Miao Ying sailing to the aid of the Old World from Fu Hung, the capital of Cathay's Southern Provinces, I imagined her brother, Li Dao, the Fire Dragon, sending a fleet of his own alongside hers.

As such, my Cathayans have been painted in reds and yellows, evoking their patron’s fiery spirit. The reds were basecoated Word Bearers Red and given a wash of Berserker Bloodshade with a Mephiston Red drybrush and highlight. The brighter yellows were used sparingly as spot colours, achieved with a Casandora Yellow wash over an Averland Sunset base, and highlighted with Yriel Yellow.

Having swapped the Battle Standard Bearer from the Core Set for an Astromancer to bring some magical support (they use Elementalism in games of Battle March, as is appropriate for a servant of the Fire Dragon!), I'm already planning my next units. My goal is to paint up a pair of Peasant Levy units as an alternative to the Grand Cannon, swapping heavy firepower for even more massed infantry.

Mark – Dwarfen Mountain Holds

With this army, my goal was to paint a solid core quickly, and then add to it later as new units are completed. With this in mind, I chose a simple paint scheme with not too many different colours. First I sprayed the models with Runelord Brass and washed them all with a 50/50 mix of Ratling Grime and Garaghak’s Sewer to pick out details. With a solid base colour for my models’ armour completed, I switched to painting five at a time, fixing the models to a strip of thick card and completing all five before moving on to the next batch.

I'm pleased with how the hand-painted banner designs came out. Little touches like this really make an army your own. I’m not sure what I’ll paint next and don’t really have a points limit in mind. I always paint the models I like the most, then write a muster list from what’s in my collection ahead of each game.

Christian – Beastmen Brayherds

For this army, I wanted to concentrate on models I love, but that would also be quick to paint. I already knew I wanted a strong contrast between model and base, so I opted for a red scheme with classic green basing.

The models were primed Chaos Black, then given a zenithal spray of White Scar. Over this I used mainly Contrast paints – Fyreslayer Flesh for the skin, Black Legion and Wyldwood for the fur, Gore-Grunta Fur and Snakebite Leather for the leather details, and Flesh Tearers Red for the red. The bases are more elaborate on the characters and elite units, but all of them feature fallen branches and tree trunks, represented by sticks and twigs I picked up whilst walking the dog. Details like these add volume to the bases and help to tell the story of a herd of Beastmen emerging from the depths of the forest.

Thanks, folks! As you can see, you can start with a Battle March Army box or create your own muster list to make your force for Battle March games. The Tomb Kings of Khemri join in the fun tomorrow when their Battle March Army box goes on pre-order, and you can prepare by downloading their army muster list right now.

download now

item.title: Designers’ notes: Night Goblin Blood Bowl team
item.description: Tips, tactics, and training plans for coaches of the newest fantasy football squad.
item.content:encoded:
If you like your games of fantasy football filled with madness, mayhem, and teeth, you’ll love the new Blood Bowl team. We hopped over to the Design Studio to get the lowdown on the new Squigs (and their Night Goblin assistants).

Tom: A never-before-seen team comes to Blood Bowl in the form of the Night Goblins. These wacky, unhinged Goblins have lingered in the background of the lore for a long time – Fanatics actually originate from Night Goblin ‘ingenuity’! Now they’re stepping into the limelight themselves – we’ve made sure it’s on a low light setting of course!

While regular Goblin teams have long run amok upon the field, Night Goblins bring their own brand of madness to the fore. Firstly, there are the Squigs. These bulbous, bouncing balls of hunger and rage are vicious opponents and diverse in their abilities. It’s not just typical Cave Squigs that you’ll have to face from Night Goblin teams, but also the speedy, bouncing Hoppers and frenzied wrecking balls that pull their Wranglers in every direction.

All this Squig action sounds too good to be true? Well, there is the tiny issue of Squig aggression to deal with. This is expressed through the new Squig Rage trait, which can result in your Squigs choosing to take a bite out of whoever is standing next to them – friend or foe – instead of immediately obeying you. Luckily, you have some tools to mitigate this!

Squig Herders

“Do they have good hearing, Jim? Everyone seems to be talking about the Squig heard!” – Bob

If there’s a lynchpin of the Night Goblin team, it's Squig Herders. The reason for this is the Squig Restraint rule, which allows their Squig teammates who are nearby to ignore Squig Rage. Careful positioning of your Herders is a must, both for total Squig coverage and because they’ll be a prime target for your opponents. The Herder’s Fend skill will help keep them a little safer – turns out having a big pointy object is good for keeping both Squigs and opposing Blood Bowl players at bay!

Linemen are the rank and file of a Night Goblin team, offering a cheap way to round out your roster. With Dodge and Stunty, they can slip through an opposing player’s grasp and they also have some extra Skills up their cavernous sleeves. The irritating personalities of the average Night Goblin are expressed through Taunt and Shadowing, offering tactical tools to scupper your opponent’s plans. An opposing player wants to create a gap? Make them follow you! They want to get away? Follow them wherever they go! Sure, it’ll result in the likely loss of an extra Night Goblin or two, but did we mention they’re cheap?

Ah, the quintessential Squig. With an impressive Strength 4 and Frenzy, Cave Squigs are the perfect tool for removing opposing players from the pitch. Being Squigs they have Pogo and Jump Up too, which combined with an AV 9+ makes them hard to keep down. You can also use Monstrous Mouth to pin a player in place – presumably to be eaten by the second Cave Squig!

You might see a small Squig and think it would be less of a problem. Well, you’d be wrong. Squig Wranglers are literal wrecking balls, with the miniature Squig dragging their handlers to and fro across the battlefield. With the Ball & Chain Trait, Night Goblin teams have two Strength 7 death dealing machines to unleash. Of course, a Goblin team wouldn’t be complete without the chance to bring onboard a hulking Troll! The perfect addition to a team during the later stages of a league, a Trained Troll adds extra hitting power to the team, and another choice when deciding how to build your starting roster. You can also throw Night Goblin Lineman in search of those cheeky touchdowns!

Night Goblin Playstyle

Night Goblins are part Stunty team, part violence-oriented. The various types of Squigs you can field provide a toolkit for removing opposing players and scoring those important touchdowns. Meanwhile, your Linemen can screen your Herders from harm and just generally be a nuisance.

Ultimately the goal of a Night Goblin team is to cause havoc, then exploit that havoc to secure victory. Use your Wranglers and Cave Squigs to break open carefully constructed defensive lines. Your Hoppers, which make ideal ball carriers, can then bounce on through. Even in those games where your Squigs prove harder to control, there’s no need to despair – you’ll be having a maddeningly fun time regardless!

Thanks, folks! Every game with the Night Goblin team will be one to remember, and you can pre-order yours from Saturday, along with the Blood Bowl legends, Ripper Bolgrot and Fungus the Loon. We’ll also have the new Blood Bowl FAQ dropping soon right here on Warhammer Community, so watch out for that too!

item.title: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard rules
item.description: Learn about the new options for the Kingdom of Bretonnia and Tomb Kings of Khemri.
item.content:encoded:
The imminent arrival of Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard brings new content for all players of Warhammer: the Old World, in particular the bold defenders of Bretonnia and the cadaverous servants of Nehekhara. To find out more about the rules contained within, we ventured into the Warhammer Studio in search of the writers.

JTY: Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard contains a wealth of new rules for Tomb Kings of Khemri and Kingdom of Bretonnia players alike, as well as four exciting new scenarios that allow players to recreate the key battles of the baron’s quest.

The first recreates the Bretonnians’ landing upon the ancient docks of Zandri and their attempt to escape that benighted city-port before the dead that populate it can gather. This is a Battle March scenario that the attackers (the Bretonnians) will find very challenging because every time they destroy an enemy unit, there is a chance an identical unit will arrive from reserve.

Dave: In the second scenario, the Bretonnians find themselves beset from all sides by Undead monstrosities as they cross the empty deserts of the Land of the Dead. The third recreates Sir Varo’s flight from Numas as he attempts to escape the clutches of the horror he has awakened.

In the final scenario, the Tomb Kings come face to face with a vast horde of Orcs and Goblins as they pursue their quarry across the Badlands. As the two armies approach one another, Sir Varo leads his knights in a glorious charge against the Undead, hoping to strike a deadly blow against the evil king that leads them and restore honour to his quest, making for a unique three-player scenario.

JTY: For Tomb Kings of Khemri players, the new content comes in the form of Dynastic Rulers and Dynastic Armies. This allows players to choose to have their army represent one of the powerful dynasties that once ruled the Great Land.

These rules give the characters that lead the army upgrades that suit the style of warfare they mastered in life. Monarchs of Nehekhara belonging to the first dynasty, which originated from Khemri, for example, have improved Weapon Skill and Initiative to reflect their martial prowess. Those belonging to the third dynasty, from Zandri, must be mounted on Skeleton Chariots, but are such skilled charioteers that they can re-roll failed dangerous terrain tests and improve the AP of their Impact Hits by 1.

Khemri – The First Dynasty

In life, as they are in death, the rulers of Nehekhara’s first and greatest city were renowned as fine and noble warriors. They were also fiercely proud, often preferring to vanquish enemies by their own hand rather than allow heralds to fight their duels.

Tomb Kings and Tomb Princes belonging to the First Dynasty have a +1 modifier to their Weapon Skill and Initiative characteristics, as well as a +1 modifier to the Armour Piercing characteristic of any non-magical weapons they wield. However, a Monarch of Nehekhara that belongs to the First Dynasty cannot decline a challenge.

Zandri – The Third Dynasty

Famed not only for its bustling docks and its construction of the vast ocean-going fleets that allowed Nehekhara to rule the waves in ancient times, Zandri also produced some of the Great Land’s finest chariots and charioteers. The noble charioteers of Zandri would spend years honing their skills in races run upon the parade grounds of sprawling palaces and temples, and even through the bustling streets of their cities. Their mastery was not limited to entertainment however, for they were also deadly warriors, able and eager to take to the battlefield when the need arose.

Tomb Kings, Tomb Princes and Royal Heralds belonging to the Third Dynasty that are mounted on Skeleton Chariots gain the First Charge special rule, and may re-roll any rolls of a 1 made when making a Dangerous Terrain test. In addition, any Impact Hits caused by these characters’ chariots have an Armour Piercing characteristic of -1.

There are similar upgrades for units as well, with those that benefit depending upon which dynasty you choose to represent. It’s a lot of fun figuring out how best to theme a Tomb Kings of Khemri army in order to make the most of each dynasty’s quirks!

Dave: For the Kingdom of Bretonnia, there’s a Questing Host Army of Infamy, inspired by Lord Carrard and his bold quest into the heart of Nehekhara. Anyone using this Army of Infamy can field a unit or two of Questing Knights amongst their Core choices, but it’s the way the army interacts with Pledges of Honour that make this army really exciting.

These are new upgrades available to knightly units and characters. In most armies, only models with the Questing Vow can swear a Pledge of Honour. But in a Questing Host, all models with a Knightly Vow can!

Pledges of Honour represent the types of pledge the knights of Bretonnia often swear on the eve of battle – noble boasts and chivalrous promises made to the Lady of the Lake. Models that fulfil their pledges during the battle gain Victory Point bonuses at its end. For example, a character that has sworn the Pledge of Conquest earns 50 VP if they are within the enemy’s deployment zone at the end of the battle. A unit that has sworn the Pledge of Protection earns 50 VP if it controls an objective when the battle ends.

Pledge Of Conquest

“By my hand, evil shall be vanquished and the lands it has conquered will be reclaimed.”

Should the character that swore this noble pledge be within your opponent’s deployment zone at the end of the battle, you win a bonus of 50 Victory Points.

Pledge Of Protection

“By our efforts the field will be won, and the enemy will be driven into the wilderness.”

0-1 per Army. If the unit that swore this knightly pledge is controlling an objective (such as a treasure trove, a baggage train, a special feature, a battlefield quarter, etc.) at the end of the battle, you win a bonus of 50 Victory Points.

As a long-time Bretonnia player, I’ve always said that chivalry is its own reward, but now there’s an actual reward – Victory Points!

Thanks, folks! The new Arcane Journal is available to pre-order on Saturday, along with a veritable legion of Tomb Kings of Khemri miniatures. In the meantime, learn more about the lore of the supplement.

item.title: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
item.description: Learn about the background of the Bretonnian baron’s fateful quest.
item.content:encoded:
The latest Arcane Journal, The Doom of Lord Carrard, will be available to pre-order this weekend. To find out more, we undertook our own quest into the depths of the Warhammer studio to speak to the designers about the lore of the latest supplement.

JTY: Since the release of Warhammer: The Old World, we’ve been following the events of Settra the Imperishable’s war against the Old World. We’ve seen his armies advance through the Border Princes and navigate the peaks and valleys of the Vaults en route to the borders of Bretonnia. We’ve even seen what happens when an ancient Liche Priest leads an army of the Undead into the depths of Athel Loren. But what we haven’t covered in much detail is what caused all this turmoil in the first place.

In Arcane Journal – the Doom of Lord Carrard we decided to address this. We wanted to explore the charnel realm of Nehekhara in greater detail, and we felt Lord Carrard’s quest allowed us to do just that.

Much of the narrative is told from the perspective of the Bretonnians, giving us a relatable lens through which to view the horrors of the Land of the Dead. This allowed us to introduce Lord Carrard himself, a baron from the realm of Brionne, and establish his relationship with Sir Lothar of Kasos Rock, once a noble knight of Carrard’s court but now an outcast dwelling in the Border Princes.

It is the arrival of a messenger from Sir Lothar that sets in motion the events that are to follow. Bringing the grim forebodings from Sir Lothar’s court, the messenger warns of a great evil stirring in the Land of the Dead and implores Lord Carrard for his aid in vanquishing it. Rather than muster armies on the strength of vague portents, the baron elects to undertake a quest, riding in the company of his closest companions to the court of his former friend.

The next part of the story is told through the recollections of Sir Varo, one of the few to return and bring word of Lord Carrard’s fate, and of the evil that has been awakened in the Land of the Dead. Through Varo we learn of the Bretonnians’ journey to the accursed city of Zandri, from where we explore Nehekhara itself, coming face to face with the horrors of the Land of the Dead as the bold knights cross the deserts and battle the undead horrors placed before them. Accompanied by a wealth of stunning new art, this tale casts a whole new light upon this accursed realm, giving the reader a sense of the scale of the civilisation that once ruled the deserts of the Great Land, and the horrors a traveller might encounter in deserts haunted by looming horrors beneath skies shrouded behind impregnable dust storms.

But that’s not all. Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard also examines ancient Nehekhara, in particular the major cities of that once-vibrant land, and the royal dynasties that once ruled over them. Delving into such ancient history was a fun challenge, and reading about the cities and dynasties of the Land of the Dead will hopefully inspire readers. There are lots of ideas here for theming your own collections of Tomb Kings of Khemri to reflect the armies of a particular city or monarch.

It’s always fun to explore the World of Legend, and shining a light on the events that led to Settra's climactic invasion was especially enjoyable. This was a story we were keen to tell, and we can’t wait to see how it will inspire readers!

Thanks, JTY! The new Arcane Journal is available for pre-order from Saturday, along with a wealth of reinforcements for the Tomb Kings of Khemri in the form of Skeleton Warriors, Skeleton Archers, Horsemen and Horse Archers, and Skeleton Chariots. Join us later in the week when we’ll be learning more about the rules in the Arcane Journal.

item.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar November update
item.description: New rules changes for your Mortal Realms armies.
item.content:encoded:
It’s time for the latest rules update for Warhammer Age of Sigmar, with a few small changes for Ossiarch Bonereapers, Khazalite Holds, and Cities of Sigmar.

Ossiarch Bonereapers

The Lance of Ossia Army of Renown has been given a small tweak to remove the extra Relentless Discipline cost for reinforced units, so that they’re more in line with the rest of the faction. Great news for Arch-Kavalos Zandtos and his indomitable horsemen.

Khazalite Holds

Everyone’s favourite unstoppable Slayer Gotrek has seen his Regiment of Renown points adjusted a bit. It means you can still take him in your Order Grand Alliance forces, but you’re paying the price for potential synergies. 

Other Changes

Beyond these notable changes, a few factions have had some rules clarified and common questions answered. The way Kharadron airships interact with troops in the Throngankor Alliance has been cleared up, and FAQ documents for the Skaven, Cities of Sigmar, and Lumineth Realm-lords have been updated.

Check out the new rules updates now, and we’ll see you again soon for the next update!

item.title: The Adepta Sororitas make their presence known in Warhammer 40,000: Darktide
item.description: Step into the boots of a Novitiate in an upcoming DLC.
item.content:encoded:
The citizens of Tertium have prayed for deliverance, and now the God-Emperor provides as the Sisters Novitiate will join Warhammer 40,000: Darktide as a new playable class.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Play as one of the pious Sisters Novitiate and flood the hive with faith and fire in a new DLC launching on 7 December, alongside a free update adding the iconic meltagun to the Novitiate and Veteran classes. 

The Sister Novitiate plays unlike any of the classes released so far, as rather than blitz and combat abilities they may choose any two of six Acts of Faith to unleash against the heretic hordes, powered by their accumulated Faith. Exactly how you generate that Faith depends on your talent tree choices, with several Devotions and Pledges available to customise your play style.

And what an arsenal they’ve brought to mete out the God-Emperor’s punishment – alongside the aforementioned meltagun, Novitiates can also wield the condemnor stake thrower, Ministorum hand flamer, mace of the righteous, penitent eviscerator, and Novitiate sword and shield – plenty of tools for splattering heretics in all manner of ways.

The new Sister Novitiate DLC will be available on Steam, PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S from 7 December.

item.description: A Warhammer 40,000 rules log is incoming.
item.content:encoded:
You may have noticed that the October rules update for Warhammer 40,000 didn’t appear in your app as a single smooth release. Instead, it arrived as sporadic downloads over several days.

This is our bad.

We’re sorry for any confusion this caused. We’re going to do better. Here’s Adam to explain further:

New Rules Update Log – coming with the next update

As Adam said in the video above, alongside the next version of the Warhammer 40,000 app, Warhammer Community is going to host a Rules Update Log to help explain the changes in simple terms. This log will list a summary of any rules changes along with date stamps to make it easy to track, which we hope will be particularly useful if you don’t play super regularly, and want to get caught up.

The next rules change for Warhammer 40,000 will be the quarterly balance update, set to be published the week beginning 7 December.

As a reminder, our aim with the cadence for any rules updates is that they be no more than monthly, with most changes limited to clarifications and addressing errors, and any more impactful amends limited to the quarterly balance updates. So unless your army gets a new Codex, you should really only need to check in four times a year for changes that make a substantive difference to your games.

item.title: Huge Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV game overview trailer revealed
item.description: Discover the factions, missions, maps, and more for the video game.
item.content:encoded:
We’re just weeks away from the release of Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV. Prepare for your return to Kronos with an epic, nine-minute trailer:

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

In the fourth installment of the legendary Warhammer 40,000 real-time strategy game series, you can take control of four factions – the Space Marines of the Blood Ravens and Dark Angels, Orks, Necrons, and Adeptus Mechanicus – across four campaigns comprising more than 70 thrilling missions.


In addition to the campaigns, there’s a Skirmish mode, with dozens of customisable settings, four game types, and support for up to five AI opponents, where you can hone your skills before taking the battle online across 30 multiplayer maps.

The Last Stand

Fan-favourite co-op survival mode The Last Stand is back, where you and two allies must hold the line against relentless waves of enemies. Choose from five heroes and assemble your strike force of companion units, bringing new layers of strategic depth to every run.

Whichever mode you like to play, the enhanced Painter tool means you can make every army your own. Choose from dozens of presets or create your own schemes with choices of colours, decals, and wargear – for the first time, you have complete creative control to paint your units’ armour and equipment piece-by-piece.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is due for release on 3 December 2026, but if you can’t wait until then, the Commander Edition gives players early access three days ahead of the main release. Pre-order either edition now to get a 10% discount, and prepare to begin the fight for Kronus anew.
